criteria.criterion: In model.json the t3 trigger names only an event that a claim it cites supports (c3, c31, c37). It does not say the agent accepts or records the worker's report unless a cited claim says so. Its trigger_evaluated_by value matches the actor the claims name.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff and claims.json. The new t3 trigger is "a PR-based worker's ready PR is recorded by the PR-check script, or a local-only worker stops with a clean ready branch". c31's source says "the pr= line bin/fm-pr-check.sh records", c3 says a place frees "when a worker records its ready PR", c32 says "its ready PR is recorded", and c37 says "the worker stops with a clean ready branch". The agent no longer appears as the subject. The fields are trigger_actor "process" and trigger_evaluated_by "code", which match the script and worker named in the claims. Caveat: c37 is prose-only, so no cited claim says code evaluates the local-only half (minor finding).

criteria.criterion: The model records each transition's trigger actor in a field, not in the trigger text. Every cited claim id exists in claims.json.
criteria.evidence: All 11 transitions in model.json get a trigger_actor (agent or process). Transition in crates/athena-cap-study/src/model.rs has deny_unknown_fields, and it gains an optional trigger_actor of type Option<Actor>. The test every_agent_decided_transition_of_the_real_study_has_the_agent_as_trigger_actor runs check_trigger_actors on the real study, which resolves every cited claim id against claims.json, and it passed.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test. The site test checks structurally, with no text prefix or keyword ban: for each transition with trigger_evaluated_by 'agent', the actor field says agent, and every cited claim id resolves. All tests pass.
criteria.evidence: The old test, which matched words and banned phrases in the trigger text, is removed. check_trigger_actors compares only the trigger_evaluated_by and trigger_actor fields and resolves claim ids against the known set. render() calls it. 31 xtask site tests passed. Athena's record shows the full suite passed (1429 tests).

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test. A fixture with an agent-evaluated transition whose trigger describes another actor's event is rejected by the check, and a fixture with a valid agent trigger passes. The tests assert both outcomes.
criteria.evidence: an_agent_decided_transition_whose_trigger_event_is_by_another_actor_is_rejected asserts an error containing "decided by the agent" for actor process, and an error when the actor is missing. an_agent_decided_transition_with_the_agent_as_trigger_actor_passes asserts Ok for agent/agent and for code/process. a_transition_citing_an_unknown_claim_is_rejected covers claim resolution. All passed. These tests exercise a function the base did not have, so they could not pass without the change.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo run -p xtask -- site. The study builds and validates, and the generated page keeps the in-scope glossary entry and a next-step link before the first transition card. It has no f2/f3 model-limit note.
criteria.evidence: `cargo run -p xtask -- site` succeeded and wrote target/verify/site/index.html. The tests in_scope_is_defined_in_the_start_terms_and_the_glossary_with_a_citation and a_link_to_the_next_step_comes_before_the_first_transition_card pass on the real study, so the glossary entry and next-step link are kept. f2 is gone. But studies/firstmate-work-handling/findings.json still holds f3 with kind "model-limit". The render loop (site.rs, around lines 501-509) prints every finding with its kind_label, so the page shows f3 tagged "what this page cannot show", which is a model-limit note. I read this from the code and the data. I did not open the generated HTML, which lies outside the working directory. The existing test only asserts that the raw string "model-limit" is absent.

criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, and clippy with -D warnings passed.

findings.summary: Two files changed outside the expected deliverables.
findings.evidence: Neither file is on the deliverables list. The change was needed: Transition has #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], so the schema had to accept trigger_actor, and the accepted reading assumed the schema would change. Meanwhile claims.json was listed but not changed, which is fine.

findings.summary: The changelog says c37 is now cited, but t3 already cited it.
findings.evidence: Base t3 claims were [c10, c11, c32, c37]. Only c3 and c31 are new.

findings.summary: No cited claim says code evaluates t3's local-only half.
findings.evidence: c37 is marked [prose-only] and says the worker stops with a clean ready branch. It does not say a script detects that. trigger_evaluated_by "code" is supported for the PR half (c31, fm-pr-check.sh) but only implied for the local-only half.

findings.summary: The 'valid' fixture's trigger text describes a non-agent event.
findings.evidence: The fixture's trigger is always "the merge lands", including in the accepted agent/agent case. That is consistent with a purely structural check, but a fixture whose text names an agent event would show intent more clearly.

summary: The candidate fails, on one criterion. The main fix is right. The t3 trigger now names only events its cited claims support: the PR-check script records a ready PR (c3, c31, c32), or a local-only worker stops with a clean ready branch (c37). It is marked trigger_actor "process", decided by "code". Every transition now has a trigger_actor field. A new check, check_trigger_actors, runs inside the site render. It rejects an agent-decided transition whose actor is not the agent, a missing or unknown actor, and a citation of a claim that does not exist. Fixtures cover both the rejected and the accepted case. The targeted tests pass, the site builds, and fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's records. Criterion 5 is not met as written: the page must have "no f2/f3 model-limit note", but findings.json still holds f3, a model-limit finding. The renderer prints every finding, so the page shows f3 under the tag "what this page cannot show". This candidate does not touch findings.json, so the base renders f3 too. That criterion may be worded wrongly, but as written it fails. Smaller findings: two crates files changed outside the deliverables list (the schema needed them), the changelog calls c37 "now cited" although t3 already cited it, and "decided by code" is not backed by any cited claim for the local-only half of t3.
